deferred_source_units.reason: The opening identifies Eliphaz as respondent; his prior identification alone is not retained as a separate connection beyond the substantive speech comparisons.

The supplied question puts fear, hope and innocence in relation to foolishness; it is not rewritten as the familiar assertion that piety is confidence, and no independently established particular target is retained.
The claim that offenders perish through the Lord's command and angry breath remains Eliphaz's account. No further particular episode or identical divine breath is assigned to it.
The extinguished strength and voices of lions and dragons are not assigned to named rulers, nations or people without evidence for those allegorical identities.
The actual ant-lion wording and separated lion cubs are preserved; the creature is not silently replaced by an old lion to manufacture a parallel.

The shaking bones and trembling describe Eliphaz's reported reaction. The surrounding nocturnal comparison is retained elsewhere, but this bodily detail establishes no separate visitor or vision identity.
The spirit upon the face and shuddering flesh do not identify a divine, angelic or demonic visitor; no such attribution is retained.
The account says Eliphaz did not recognize it and saw no form, while hearing a breeze and voice. The separately read Elijah candidate does not establish the identity or authority of this visitor.
The reported voice's distrust of servants and crookedness in angels does not identify the angels with the imprisoned sinful angels in the separately read candidate.
The challenge about obtaining an answer or seeing holy angels supplies no named intermediary or independently established angelic episode.
Eliphaz's statement about a fool's sons being unrescued and battered is not equated with Job's children's different narrated catastrophe or used to pronounce them guilty.
The righteous eating what was gathered, the absence of rescue and drained strength are preserved as Eliphaz’s claims; no additional specific transfer of property or harvest is identified.
The denial that toil comes out of the earth or pain sprouts from mountains is not turned into a literal geographical claim or used to establish a cause for Job's suffering.
Eliphaz announces his own recourse to the Lord; a generic parallel involving prayer would add no sufficiently particular connection, and his first-person wording is preserved.
The six-and-seven assurance is not matched to an arbitrary count of Job's losses or to a different sevenfold saying as though they count the same events.
The assurance about a peaceful house and unfailing tent livelihood is not assigned an exact house, tent or later incident solely from a general restoration theme.
The introduction marks Job's reply; its speaker transition is read as necessary context without adding a separate identity-only link.
The unceasing soul and food described as a lion-like stench retain this version's imagery; they are not changed into a familiar description of tasteless food to make a comparison.
The request for hope to be granted is read with the following plea not to be destroyed completely. Its unspecified request is not automatically converted into an unqualified wish to be killed.
The questions about strength and remaining time express Job's endurance problem, but no additional particular comparison beyond the nearby retained bodily-strength image is selected.
Job's stated trust and distance from help remain part of his complaint; a generic verse about seeking help would not supply an independently particular connection.
The hostile approach likened to frozen snow and ice is not normalized into a different torrent or caravan reading; no specific group or incident is assigned.
The melting-snow image explains the surrounding abandonment complaint, but a general observation that snow melts is not retained as a separate cross-reference.
The Temanite roads and Sabean paths do not identify the earlier unnamed raiders. That separately read candidate remains unresolved and receives no credit.
Job denies asking the visitors for something or needing their strength; no particular payment, gift or later donation is identified as the thing he denies seeking.
The question about rescue from enemies and rulers continues the preceding denial of a request; it is not changed into a narrated ransom or capture episode.
The comment on supposedly worthless truthful words and not asking for strength remains in the argument. The more specific reciprocal endurance-of-words comparison is retained for 6:26 instead.
Job's appeal to their faces and denial of lying do not establish a separate episode or oath; the fuller later defense of truthful speech is connected to 6:30.
The appeal to sit without injustice and associate again with a righteous person is preserved as Job's plea, without assigning a separate tribunal or declaring a new social identity.
The empty months and nights of pain give the complaint's duration, but no separately numbered period or dated illness is inferred.
The actual comparison of life with chatter is not replaced by a weaver's shuttle. No independent particular connection is retained on that absent wording.
The anticipated disappearance from human and divine sight remains Job's lament. No distinct disappearance or vision episode is identified from this statement alone.
Job's hope of comfort on a bed introduces the following frightening dreams; its ordinary bed image is not retained as an additional independent connection.
The actual release of soul from breath and bones from death is preserved. It is not rewritten as choosing strangling or preferring death, and no target is retained on those absent words.
The request for forgetfulness of wrongdoing and cleansing before departure is read as Job's appeal. A generic forgiveness verse is not retained without a more particular established connection.
The heading introduces Bildad's reply; identification with the already introduced visitor alone supplies no additional substantive comparison.
The anticipated teaching from earlier generations continues 8:8. No particular unnamed ancestor or independent saying is identified beyond that retained appeal.
The unharvested plant's withering continues Bildad's water-dependent illustration; it is not equated with a particular crop failure or subjected to an invented chronology.
The supplied wording about moisture, sun and a shoot from decay is preserved without replacing it with a familiar flourishing plant description or assigning a named person to the image.
The person lying among stones and pebbles is not rewritten as roots wrapped around rocks; no geographical location or botanical identity is invented.
The overthrow and another sprouting from earth remain Bildad's illustration; no particular successor, dynasty or new righteous generation is identified.

same_chapter_policy: No retained same-chapter links are present; every retained connection crosses the source chapter boundary or a book boundary.
textual_precision_notes: Eliphaz speaks in4-5, Job replies in6-7, and Bildad speaks in8; the prologue and42:7-8 qualify how the friends’ disputed inferences are presented. Wisdom parallels do not establish Job’s guilt, and the later citation of5:13 does not vindicate the whole speech.
The actual ant-lion, vulture, chatter, grave-and-city and release-from-death wording remains; no old-lion, sparks, weaver’s-shuttle, caravans or preference-for-strangling wording is imported.
The source’s request in6:9 explicitly stops short of complete destruction; the different agents in2:6 and6:9 are preserved.
Job14:10-15 is read through its explicit hope of life again;42:17a is a distinct closing resurrection notice, not silently omitted to impose uniform finality on7:9.
Psalms102:16 says the human no longer recognizes his place, the reverse grammatical direction of Job7:10 and8:18. Both retained comparisons state that difference.
Hosea’s beast-covenant target is2:20 in this actual source numbering. Psalms use the supplied numbering, including142,125,131 and77.

Proverbs14:30 does not mention jealousy in this pinned version; the initial possible comparison was discarded, and5:2 instead uses the explicitly matching Sirach30:24. Isaiah40:6-8 does not include a divine-breath clause and was not used to supply one.
Job9:25 does not include the word good; no link imports it. Job40:15-18 gives a grass-eating creature without supplying a species name, and its ribs and spine remain distinct from Job’s flesh in6:12.

The report in4:16 says no form was seen; the unretained candidate and source reason were corrected to state that, with all earlier versions preserved. The visitor, angelic referent and Sabean-raider identity remain unresolved.

Seven retained-row refinements are precisely preserved and all corrected complete triples personally reread. The five source-reason changes include two precision improvements and three spacing fixes; the one candidate wording change was separately reread.
